title: Plant growth‐promoting rhizobacteria improve growth, photosynthetic efficiency and antioxidant response of quinoa plants under hyperosmotic salinity
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

Soil salinity severely limits crop productivity worldwide, and plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) offer a sustainable strategy to enhance plant tolerance to salt stress. Although quinoa (Chenopodium quinoa Willd.) is inherently salt tolerant, the physiological mechanisms underlying PGPR-mediated improvement under hyperosmotic salinity remain poorly understood, particularly the coordination between photosynthetic energy use and oxidative stress regulation. This study investigated the effects of soil inoculation with Hartmannibacter diazotrophicus strain E19T on growth, photosynthetic performance, water-use efficiency (WUE), redox status and ion balance of quinoa exposed to 300 mmol L−1 NaCl.

RESULTS

Salinity without PGPR markedly increased oxidative stress markers (proline, malondialdehyde, H2O2) and antioxidant enzyme activities (superoxide dismutase, catalase, ascorbate peroxidase), while reducing biomass, chlorophyll content, CO₂ assimilation (A net) and WUE. Inoculation with E19T significantly enhanced growth parameters, increasing the fresh biomass of leaves and roots by 28% and 25%, respectively, as well as total plant fresh weight, mitigated chlorophyll degradation, enhanced A net (78%) and WUE (45%) and decreased the electron transport rate/A net ratio, indicating more efficient photochemical energy allocation to carbon assimilation rather than reactive oxygen species detoxification. Correspondingly, enzymatic and nonenzymatic oxidative stress indicators decreased, and leaf nutrient balance improved. Notably, qPCR revealed high root colonization by E19T, approximately 6.5-fold greater than previously observed in wheat under salinity, highlighting its versatility and a marked affinity for quinoa.

CONCLUSION

Soil inoculation with H. diazotrophicus E19T effectively mitigates the negative impacts of hyperosmotic salinity on quinoa, enhancing growth, photosynthetic efficiency and oxidative stress. These findings provide a mechanistic framework for the use of PGPR as a sustainable strategy to improve halophytic crop performance under salinized soils. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
